scope: Recover the isolated 8216 native App Server after its fixed Primary credential could no longer refresh, without modifying 8215 or sending a model request.

failure_evidence.app_server_log: The provider refresh returned HTTP 401 and the sanitized App Server auth status reported auth_token_missing.
failure_evidence.credential_boundary: The App Server systemd credential matched the fixed Primary binding while the router route was Secondary. No credential bytes, identity, token, cookie, email or full provider response were recorded.

repair.credential_install: Atomically installed the existing root-owned Secondary router credential as the fixed 8216 App Server credential with mode 0600 and a rollback copy in /run.
repair.reason_web_restart_was_required: The Web process did not reconnect to the replacement App Server Unix socket after the App Server-only restart; the Web restart established a new IPC bridge and invalidated only 8216 browser sessions.

residual_risks: The isolated App Server still has one fixed systemd credential. Router-only manual or automatic route changes do not persistently rebind that native App Server identity.
A future expiry of the fixed Secondary credential can return the native App Host to the login screen even if another router credential remains usable.

Making native App Server identity follow every route change would expand the approved root helper beyond its current catalog/credential-store/account-router-only restart boundary and requires a separate least-privilege design and authorization.
Optional Statsig requests still time out in the browser-control channel but did not block the verified composer.
